ABB India Q2 FY27: Strong Profit Growth Masks Margin Pressure as Premium Valuation Tests Limits
sum: Following the results announcement, the stock traded at ₹7,045.00 on November 13, 2026, gaining 1.37% on the day and demonstrating resilience despite the margin concerns. However, at 78 times trailing twelve-month earnings and trading well above the sector's average price-to-earnings ratio of 48, investors face a critical question: can ABB India's operational excellence justify its premium valuation, or are margin pressures signalling a turning point for this market leader?

The quarterly performance reflects ABB India's ability to capitalise on robust demand in India's infrastructure and electrification sectors, with revenue reaching an all-time quarterly high. Yet beneath this topline strength lies a narrative of margin compression and profitability challenges that warrant closer scrutiny from investors evaluating entry points at current valuations.
Financial Performance: Revenue Momentum Meets Margin Headwinds

ABB India's Q2 FY27 revenue performance demonstrates impressive momentum, with net sales climbing to ₹3,738.13 crores from ₹3,558.87 crores in Q1 FY27, representing a 5.04% sequential increase. The year-on-year comparison proves even more compelling, with revenue surging 19.42% from ₹3,130.11 crores in Q2 FY26, underscoring robust demand across the company's electrification, automation, and motion portfolios.

However, the profitability picture reveals concerning trends. Operating profit before depreciation, interest, and tax (excluding other income) stood at ₹551.98 crores with a margin of 14.91%, whilst improving sequentially from 12.70% in Q1 FY27, this represents a significant contraction from the 15.64% achieved in Q2 FY25 and falls well short of the 18.71% margin recorded in Q4 FY25. The compression suggests rising input costs or competitive pricing pressures that management has struggled to offset through operational efficiencies.

The consolidated net profit of ₹442.52 crores marked a 22.14% quarter-on-quarter improvement from ₹362.30 crores, yet the year-on-year growth of merely 8.19% from ₹409.04 crores indicates that profit expansion has lagged revenue growth substantially. This divergence between topline momentum and bottom-line delivery raises questions about the sustainability of current profit margins in an environment of robust revenue growth.

sum: ABB's planned acquisition of UK flow-control specialist Rotork has put the Swiss engineering group's portfolio strategy back at the center of the investment debate. Simply Wall St reported on November 13 that ABB had agreed to buy the UK flow-control specialist in a US$5.6 billion cash transaction.

The deal would broaden ABB's automation footprint beyond its established electrification, motion and software activities. It also reinforces a wider reshaping of the group, which includes the planned sale of its robotics business and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Electric in Asia Pacific.

The strategic case is supported by stronger operating activity. Simply Wall St said ABB's third-quarter 2026 revenue and net income were above the levels recorded in the third quarter of 2025. The same comparison showed net margin declining from 13.8 percent to 12.6 percent, leaving the effect of growth on profitability less clear.

That contrast matters for shareholders. A larger automation portfolio could improve ABB's exposure to industrial investment, grid resilience and data-center infrastructure, but the company must also convert that demand into durable earnings. The Rotork transaction adds execution and integration requirements at a time when investors are already assessing the consequences of the robotics divestment.
ABB stock traded at 76.16 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:33 CET on Friday, November 13.

The immediate investor question is whether ABB can sustain demand in electrification and automation while absorbing a large acquisition and completing the robotics transaction. The margin decline keeps the focus on earnings quality rather than headline sales growth alone.

ABB stock takes third hybrid ferry role in Washington program
sum: ABB will supply and integrate the power and propulsion system for a third hybrid-electric newbuild ferry for Washington State Ferries, extending its role in the program from two vessels to three. MarineLink reported the development on Wednesday, November 11, citing ABB information dated October 29.

The vessel will use ABB's Onboard DC Grid and Power and Energy Management System. The solution is designed to coordinate available power sources and energy storage, reducing reliance on diesel engines during operation. ABB will also provide marine automation, propulsion drives and motors, transformers, low-voltage systems, uninterruptible power supplies, remote diagnostics, propulsion shafting, propellers, steering gear and rudders, as well as engineering and commissioning support.

The integrated battery system has a capacity of 13.2 megawatt-hours. It is designed to enable all-electric, zero-emission operation on short routes and while the ferry is in port. Washington State Ferries burns about 19 million gallons of diesel each year, according to the MarineLink report, while its electrification program targets lower emissions through 2040.

The third vessel forms part of a broader plan for up to 16 hybrid-electric ferries by 2040. ABB's involvement therefore extends beyond a single delivery and gives its marine electrification business another reference project in the United States. The report does not provide a contract value or delivery date.

sum: In a significant move signaling changes in the robotics sector, ABB has announced its decision to divest its Robotics division to SoftBank Group Corp. for an enterprise value of $5.375 billion. This agreement, revealed in October 2025, is part of ABB’s strategic initiatives aimed at enhancing its focus on electrification and automation technologies.

The successful completion of this transaction hinges on obtaining necessary regulatory approvals and fulfilling customary closing conditions. SoftBank is tasked with managing the process of securing these approvals. However, complications have arisen, notably with the Office of the Working Mechanism for Foreign Investment Security Review in China, which has prohibited SoftBank from acquiring ABB’s Robotics business within the country. Despite this setback, both companies remain engaged in constructive discussions to navigate the challenges associated with the transaction.

ABB has established itself as a global technology leader with a rich history spanning over 140 years, employing approximately 110,000 people across the globe. The firm is recognized for its commitment to providing sustainable and efficient solutions that empower industries to perform at their best while also promoting resource efficiency. The company’s mantra, “Engineered to Outrun,” reflects its goal of leveraging engineering and digitalization expertise to help customers improve efficiency, productivity, and sustainability.

Investors and stakeholders are closely watching this transaction as it unfolds, given its potential impact on the robotics landscape and the strategic directions of both ABB and SoftBank. ABB Keeps Buying Back Stock While Beijing Blocks Its Robotics Sale
sum: ABB repurchased 575,000 of its own shares between 29 October and Wednesday, the Swiss engineering group said Thursday, continuing a buyback programme it announced on 6 February. Cumulative purchases since the programme began on 9 February now total 12,593,273 shares.

The buyback runs alongside a far less settled matter: the sale of ABB's robotics business to SoftBank, which China's outbound investment security review body has blocked. SoftBank informed ABB of the decision, and ABB said the two companies remain in close dialogue and are working constructively on the transaction. The agreed deal carries an enterprise value of USD 5.375bn.

Swiss broadcaster SRF floated two possible routes forward — a restructuring of the transaction, or a separate buyer for the China units. Neither has been resolved, and the outcome of the sale remains open. Media reports have questioned whether the agreed disposal can close at all; Reuters reported a decline in ABB shares on Thursday tied to the Chinese veto, with market commentary pointing to uncertainty over the deal and ABB's China business.

Analysts have kept their footing even as the deal wobbles. UBS reaffirmed its "Neutral" rating on Wednesday with a price target of CHF 88, as reported by dpa-AFX — a confirmation rather than an upgrade or downgrade. Analyst Andre Kukhnin based the call on findings from a conversation with ABB chief executive Morten Wierod, whose tone the study described as confident. Goldman Sachs, by contrast, cut its target on 30 October to CHF 79 from CHF 82 while holding its "Neutral" rating. Same stance, different numbers.

Away from the transaction, ABB on Monday reported two orders from Southwest Aluminum (Group) Co., Ltd. covering integrated automation, process control and digital solutions for two cold rolling mills in Chongqing. Both plants are scheduled to be fully operational by the end of 2027.

In a separate regulatory disclosure, a member of ABB's management acquired 170 ABB registered shares on 31 October under the Employee Share Acquisition Plan, a transaction valued at CHF 10,098 according to the SIX register filing.
The stock rose 0.8% on Friday. ABB's next confirmed event is its Group Capital Markets Day on 18 November 2026 in New Berlin, USA.

sum: ABB has run into a regulatory roadblock that could reshape a deal worth billions. The Swiss engineering group confirmed that China's foreign investment security review authority has blocked SoftBank's acquisition of ABB's robotics operations inside China, a decision first reported by Reuters. The prohibition targets the Chinese portion of the business, yet it casts a shadow over the wider transaction rather than amounting to a confirmed cancellation of the entire sale.

The economics behind the disposal were straightforward. ABB Robotics turned over USD 2.3 billion in 2024, roughly 7% of group revenue, while posting an operating margin of 12.1% — well short of the 18.1% managed at group level. Shedding a unit that trails the parent's profitability made strategic sense, provided the separation could be executed on workable terms.

The financial stakes were laid out when the transaction was agreed in October 2025. ABB anticipated net cash proceeds of about USD 5.3 billion after transaction costs, plus a non-operational pre-tax book gain of roughly USD 2.4 billion. The agreed enterprise value stood at USD 5.375 billion, with completion originally targeted for mid-to-late 2026.

Those projections remain contingent on closing. Both companies say they are continuing to work constructively toward the deal, which keeps a negotiated outcome alive as long as talks produce an implementable agreement. What hangs in the balance now is the structure, the proceeds and the timetable of any completed sale — and only once those are fixed can investors gauge how much of the expected benefit ABB actually retains.

China is the largest market for ABB Robotics, so the veto lands squarely on a core part of the business. According to the Financial Times, Chinese authorities worry that robotics data could flow abroad and be used to train AI models. Any revised structure that keeps the Chinese operations inside the takeover would have to address those security concerns.
Investors marked the stock down 4.3% on the news, reflecting concern that the sale is now harder to pull off. The pullback captures that uncertainty rather than any confirmed collapse of the deal.

ABB Q3 FY 2026 Earnings Show Record Orders Outpacing Revenue on Data Centers
sum: ABB’s third quarter showed demand for its electrification portfolio running well ahead of what it can deliver in the near term, with data centers again leading the way. New direct current technology and a joint venture in Japan point to where management wants the next leg of growth to come from.

The News: ABB (NYSE: ABB) reported third-quarter results for the period ended September 30, 2026. Revenue was $9.70 billion, up 14% year on year (YoY) on both a reported and comparable basis, versus consensus of $9.77 billion. By business area, Electrification revenue was $5.42 billion (up 21% YoY), Motion revenue was $2.32 billion (up 11% YoY), and Automation revenue was $2.13 billion (up 6% YoY). Orders reached a record $12.06 billion, up 40% YoY, for a book-to-bill ratio of 1.24 and an order backlog of $32.26 billion. Operational EBITA rose 24% YoY to $2.03 billion, with the margin expanding 160 basis points to 20.8%. Net income attributable to ABB was $1.18 billion, down 2% YoY, and basic earnings per share (EPS) was $0.65, down 2% YoY.

“ABB delivered record order intake and improved operational performance with strong cash flow and return on capital. We advanced our leading position in direct current technology, and today we progressed on M&A with a new electrification joint venture with Mitsubishi Electric,” said Morten Wierod, CEO of ABB.

Analyst Take: The first thing we notice here is a strong demand story: Comparable orders rose 40%, well ahead of revenue, pushing the backlog to roughly the size of ABB’s entire FY 2025 revenue base. The Operational EBITA margin was the best Q3 result in ABB’s history, yet basic EPS slipped on a non-cash hedge linked to the Rotork acquisition and a tax charge tied to separating ABB Robotics, now a discontinued operation.

Investors fixed on that dip and a slight revenue shortfall, and the shares fell as much as 6.7% on the day. I think that reaction misreads a quarter whose bigger news was the Infinitus DC launch and the Mitsubishi Electric joint venture, but also misses the point of where ABB looks to be headed.
Electrification orders also climbed 70% on a comparable basis to $7.67 billion, the seventh straight quarter of sequential growth. Note that this lifts the business area’s backlog to $16 billion.

ABB said data-center orders grew at a triple-digit rate during the quarter. Two of its three business areas contributed strongly to the increase, and demand was positive across most customer segments.

sum: Semiconductor shares across Europe, Asia and the United States tumbled on Thursday, extending a global rout in technology stocks after hotter-than-expected US inflation data rekindled bets that the Federal Reserve may need to raise interest rates further.

The selloff, which began on Wall Street and swept through Asian markets before hitting Europe, was broad-based and severe. German chipmakers Infineon and Aixtron each fell about 8% to 9% in early European trading, while Dutch equipment maker ASM International dropped by a similar margin. ASML, the region's most valuable technology company, slid 5.5% to 5.6%, and BE Semiconductor lost 5.7% to 6.5%. France's STMicroelectronics slumped 6.5% to 7.5%.

Smaller European names were hit even harder. Suss MicroTec fell as much as 9.4%, while Elmos Semiconductor and Swiss chip and lighting company ams OSRAM declined between 3.6% and 7%. Siltronic, Soitec and Technoprobe tumbled between 6.5% and 10%, and AI-exposed industrial stocks including Nokia, Legrand, Schneider Electric and ABB slid 4% to 5%.

In the US, memory chipmakers bore the brunt of the selling. SK Hynix slumped 6.7% and Micron fell 4.1% in premarket trading, while Western Digital and Seagate Technology each lost more than 4%. Nvidia, the bellwether for AI-related chip demand, slid 1.8%, and Intel and AMD dropped more than 3% each.

The catalyst for the rout came Wednesday, when the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that US consumer prices rose 0.6% in September from August, lifting the annual inflation rate to 3.7% from 3.4% a month earlier. The monthly figure matched economists' expectations, but the annual reading came in a tenth of a percentage point above the 3.6% consensus forecast.

Core inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy costs, rose 0.3% on the month and 2.6% from a year earlier, up from 2.4% in August. Both readings exceeded forecasts by a tenth of a point. Surging energy costs were once again the primary driver of the increase.

The data immediately reshaped expectations for the Fed's policy path. Traders briefly priced in roughly even odds of a rate increase at the central bank's meeting later this month before pulling those bets back.

sum: My dad loved it as a kid when I was young, and he would put Formula One on the telly and I would normally fall asleep to it, and then eventually the commentary would get exciting and wake me up and I’d sort of go, "Oh, this is quite fun". Then over the years my dad would call me in to watch the starts and so on and so forth.

I always liked motorsport as a kid, but I just never saw myself working in it. I started pursuing working in film on the media side of things, but getting as much experience as I could. I learned to edit through making fan edits of comic books and superhero films I watched. Later down the line, I ended up showing those videos in job interviews.

My actual ‘big break’ was probably when I got my apprenticeship when I was 18. I applied for apprenticeships in journalism, media production and got close but didn’t get any, apart from my last one where I worked for a company called IMG (sports media) who trained me in how to make telly, and I suddenly was working in sport, which I hadn’t seen for myself.
You were part of FE’s Talent Call all those years ago. How crucial was that program in getting you to where you are today?

Unbelievably crucial. When Formula E’s Talent Call came around, I was doing my apprenticeship, so I was very tuned into the media space and I’d done a little bit of presenting and reporting before through other youth schemes designed to get young people involved in media, but I wasn’t really sure if I could make it work as a career.

I remember going online one day and I saw a tweet about the open call for presenters and I thought to myself, well, why don’t I make a TikTok for them? Because if they want a new young presenter, they’re probably going to want someone who understands TikTok and that was something I really enjoyed.

It was the craziest, coolest experience finding out I was in the final four and we got to go to Valencia testing, which was my first time actually on the ground at a motorsport event. So not only did it provide me the opportunity to get on the ground, but also during that weekend we were tasked with presenting one minute pieces to camera and I got to interview Lucas di Grassi and that blew my mind.

sum: Intermoney | Merlin Properties (MRL) (Buy, Target Price €15) announced on Wednesday, after the market closed, a capital increase via an accelerated bookbuilding (ABB) process. The SOCIMI will issue 52.3 million shares, or 10% of the share capital, which at yesterday’s closing price would represent a capital inflow of €768 million. Both Santander and Nortia, Manuel Lao’s vehicle, with stakes in Merlin of 24.7% and 8.2% respectively, have confirmed that they will subscribe to the increase.

The new capital will be used to finance Phase III of the data centres, which will involve the development of 412 MW in Bilbao, Zaragoza and Lisbon. The REIT expects this phase to require an investment of around €4.5 billion, to be financed on a 50/50 basis through equity and the issue of corporate bonds.

Assessment: Merlin has finally issued the new shares at yesterday’s closing price, meaning the capital increase exceeds €700 million – the REIT’s stated target for this first capital increase, as outlined on 10 March at its CMD in Bilbao. In fact, we had the impression that this move would have been immediate had it not been for the conflict in the Middle East.

Once Phase III is commissioned, which the REIT expects to happen in 2031, it is estimated that 65% of revenue will come from data centres. Our current estimates only include up to Phase II, or a total of 318 MW, but even so, this would imply that EBITDA would more than double between 2025 and 2031, reaching €836 million. In our valuation, data centres already account for 25% of NAV, at around €3.2 billion.
